title: Dimension-free KLS Poincare bound for isotropic log-concave densities
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib library for Poincare inequalities, log-concave probability measures and stochastic localization. Its dimension-free KLS theorem bounds the intrinsic local-slope Poincare constant by one universal constant times the covariance operator norm, including dimension zero and singular affine supports, for log-concave probability laws with finite second moment. The proof follows Bizeul-Klartag-Lehec through finite-horizon cutoff localization, the compact Letwin constant-8 quadratic variance bound and approximation. Supporting results include Cheeger-Buser comparisons, covariance and energy interfaces and moment-map calculus. This Palomar configuration compares two density statements. Each asserts the existence of a positive constant C that works in every dimension n >= 1 and for every measurable isotropic log-concave probability density. The pinned OpenAI statement gives Var(f) <= C * E|grad f|^2 for smooth compactly supported tests and is the statement registered in PALOMAR-2026-11-01-000014 v1. The density-coordinate formulation of Bizeul-Klartag-Lehec Theorem 1.1 applies to every locally Lipschitz f in L^2 and uses an extended nonnegative squared-gradient integral that may be infinite. The locally Lipschitz definitions and bridge are new project code, not part of the OpenAI model. No numerical final KLS constant or uncut Eldan construction is claimed.
